intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Joseon-era royal palace while dressed in traditional Hanbok attire. Hanbok rental shops are located just outside the palace gates, making it easy to combine both activities. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry. Ideal for Day 2 or 3 after settling in, and best done in the morning to avoid crowds. Stay nearby in Jongno-gu to walk directly to the palace.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). The market is lively and authentic, offering a true local food experience without tourist markup. Book a guided food tour or explore independently. Stay in Jongno-gu or Euljiro for easy access.

experiences.name: Hongdae K-Culture & Street Performance Walk
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Seoul's vibrant K-pop and youth culture hub. Hongdae is packed with indie music venues, K-pop dance studios offering drop-in classes, street performers, quirky cafes, and K-beauty shops. Join a K-pop dance class at a local studio for around $15–20, then explore the nightlife and street art. This area is best experienced in the late afternoon through evening when energy peaks.

experiences.name: Insadong Teahouse & Craft Culture Experience
experiences.description: Wander through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and galleries. Visit Ssamziegil, an artsy courtyard mall with local designers and handmade goods. Stop at a traditional Korean tea house to try omija tea or sikhye. This culturally rich neighborhood is walkable from Gyeongbokgung and Gwangjang Market, making it perfect for a combined day out. Ideal for mid-trip exploration.

experiences.name: Korean BBQ Dinner Experience in Mapo-gu
experiences.description: Enjoy an authentic Korean BBQ dinner at a local grill restaurant in the Mapo-gu area near Hongdae or Hapjeong. Order samgyeopsal (pork belly) or galbi (beef short ribs), grilled tableside and wrapped in lettuce with ssamjang paste. Pair with unlimited banchan side dishes and soju or makgeolli. This is a quintessential Korean dining ritual best enjoyed with a group. Staying in Mapo-gu puts you steps away from top BBQ spots.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or bus to Bupyeong station. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store for easy transit use throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour GS25 or CU convenience store near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or a hot dog (under ₩5,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — just check in and rest. Exchange some cash at the airport (Incheon has competitive rates). Buy a T-money transit card at the airport 7-Eleven or GS25 for ₩2,500 and load ₩30,000–₩50,000 to start.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a free hotel breakfast if included, then explore Bupyeong Modoo Mall and the underground Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center — one of Korea's largest underground markets. Browse affordable K-fashion, accessories, and street snacks. Great introduction to local shopping culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Line 1) from Bupyeong to Incheon Chinatown and Jayu Park area. Walk through Korea's only Chinatown, admire the colorful murals and gates, then climb up to Jayu (Freedom) Park for panoramic views of Incheon port. Visit the nearby Open Port Area with its historic Japanese and Western colonial architecture — all free.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sinpo International Market, one of Incheon's oldest traditional markets. Try the famous Sinpo dakgangjeong (sweet fried chicken) and browse street food stalls. Return to hotel via subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store (₩2,000–₩4,000)
meals.lunch: Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) at a Chinatown restaurant — authentic and cheap (₩6,000–₩8,000)
meals.dinner: Sinpo Market street food: dakgangjeong, tteokbokki, hotteok (₩5,000–₩8,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Wear warm layers — December highs are around 3°C. The Chinatown and port area is very walkable. Subway fare from Bupyeong is around ₩1,400–₩1,600 each way with T-money.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway into central Seoul (about 50–60 min from Bupyeong via Line 1 to Seoul Station or transfer). Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace — the grandest of Seoul's five royal palaces. Arrive early for the 10:00 Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony at the main gate. Admission is ₩3,000 (free if wearing hanbok).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bukchon Hanok Village, a preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the scenic alleyways and enjoy free views of the city. Then explore Insadong, Seoul's cultural arts district — browse galleries, traditional craft shops, and quirky K-culture stores. Visit Ssamziegil, a unique open-air shopping complex with indie shops.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Insadong for dinner, then walk to nearby Tapgol Park. Head back toward Jonggak or Anguk station for the subway home. The area is beautifully lit at night in winter.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Insadong street food: hotteok (sweet pancake), tteokbokki, or a set meal at a local restaurant (₩7,000–₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong traditional Korean set meal (dosirak or bibimbap) at a local eatery (₩8,000–₩12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Hanbok rental near the palace costs ₩10,000–₩15,000 for 2 hours and grants free palace entry — great value and a fun K-culture experience. Bring hand warmers for outdoor walking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) — take Bus 02 from Chungmuro or the Namsan cable car (₩9,500 round trip) up the mountain. Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul from the observation deck (₩16,000 entry) or just enjoy the free outdoor deck and love locks for free. The mountain walk up is free if you skip the cable car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and explore Myeongdong — Seoul's most famous shopping and street food district. Browse K-beauty shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young) for affordable skincare and cosmetics. Sample the incredible street food along the main strip.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Myeongdong for dinner, then visit the nearby명동성당 (Myeongdong Cathedral), beautifully lit at night. Check out any winter festival decorations in the area. Head back to Bupyeong via subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food crawl: egg bread (gyeran-ppang), tornado potato, grilled lobster skewer, Korean corn dog (₩8,000–₩12,000 total)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja — famous and affordable kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) or mandu (dumplings), a Seoul institution (₩9,000–₩11,000)

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is very touristy but street food prices are reasonable. K-beauty products are significantly cheaper here than abroad — great for gifts. Olive Young is the best one-stop shop for affordable Korean skincare.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Gwangjang Market — one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. This is a must for food lovers. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), and yukhoe (beef tartare) at the market stalls. The market is lively and authentic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a stunning futuristic building by Zaha Hadid. Explore the free outdoor areas and any free exhibitions inside. Then visit Dongdaemun Market area for affordable clothing and fabric shopping. On weekends, the wholesale fashion markets open in the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the unique Dongdaemun night shopping culture — many fashion wholesale markets open from 8 PM onwards (Doota, Migliore). Browse affordable K-fashion. The area is buzzing on Saturday nights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market — bindaetteok + mayak kimbap + sikhye (rice drink) (₩8,000–₩12,000)
meals.dinner: Street food or a pojangmacha (street tent restaurant) near Dongdaemun for tteokbokki, sundae, and odeng (₩7,000–₩10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is open daily but most vibrant on weekends. Bring cash as many stalls don't accept cards. DDP hosts rotating free exhibitions — check their website for current shows.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). The palace costs ₩3,000 and the Secret Garden guided tour is ₩5,000 extra — worth it for the beautiful winter scenery of bare trees and traditional architecture. Tours run at set times; book ahead or arrive early.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a trendy neighborhood of renovated hanok houses turned into cafes, boutiques, and restaurants. Very photogenic and popular with locals. Browse the indie shops and enjoy the mix of traditional and modern Korean culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream — a restored urban stream running through central Seoul. Walk along the illuminated stream path, especially beautiful in winter with holiday lights. End the evening at a nearby jjimjilbang (Korean sauna) for a warm, budget-friendly relaxation session.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong cafe or small restaurant — try dosirak (Korean lunch box) or a trendy Korean fusion dish (₩9,000–₩13,000)
meals.dinner: Affordable Korean BBQ at a local restaurant near Cheonggyecheon — samgyeopsal (pork belly) sets start around ₩12,000–₩15,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung is closed on Mondays. The Secret Garden tour is in Korean but the scenery speaks for itself. Jjimjilbang entry is typically ₩10,000–₩15,000 and includes access to hot baths, saunas, and a common rest area — great for warming up on a cold winter night.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — Seoul's youth culture and indie music hub. Explore the vibrant street art, murals, and quirky shops around the university. Visit the free Hongdae street performance area and browse the unique indie boutiques and vintage clothing stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short subway ride to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area — another trendy shopping and cafe district. Browse affordable fashion and K-pop merchandise stores. Visit the beautiful Ewha campus, which has a stunning underground glass building (ECC) — free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening — the area comes alive at night with buskers, live music, and street performers. Explore the club and bar street if interested, or just enjoy the lively atmosphere. Many affordable restaurants and pojangmacha in the area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Hongdae area — try a Korean set meal (백반, baekban) at a local restaurant for great value (₩7,000–₩9,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae street food or a budget Korean restaurant — dakbal (spicy chicken feet) or budae jjigae (army stew) are local favorites (₩8,000–₩12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is one of the best areas to experience modern K-culture, K-pop, and youth fashion. Many K-pop entertainment company buildings are nearby (HYBE, JYP, YG are in the greater area). Free street performances happen most evenings near the main square.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks, located in Jamsil. A full-day ticket is around ₩62,000 but check for discount coupons on Klook or Coupang. Alternatively, the outdoor Magic Island section has great views of Seokchon Lake. The adjacent Lotte World Mall is free to browse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Lotte World or, for a budget alternative, walk around Seokchon Lake — a beautiful free outdoor area with winter scenery. Visit the nearby Lotte World Tower observation deck (₩27,000) for stunning views, or just admire the tower from outside.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jamsil's local restaurant streets for dinner. Explore the area around Jamsil Station for affordable Korean dining options. Return to hotel via subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Inside Lotte World or a nearby convenience store to save budget (₩5,000–₩8,000)
meals.dinner: Local Korean restaurant near Jamsil — galbi-tang (short rib soup) or doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) set meal (₩8,000–₩12,000)

day_by_day.notes: If Lotte World feels too expensive, skip it and spend the day at the free Seokchon Lake and Lotte World Mall instead — still a great experience. Check Klook for discounted Lotte World tickets (sometimes 20–30% off).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namdaemun Market — Seoul's largest traditional market and one of the oldest. Explore the maze of stalls selling everything from clothing and accessories to kitchenware and food. Great for affordable souvenir shopping. Try the famous Namdaemun galchi jorim (braised hairtail fish) or kalguksu.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Seoul City Hall Plaza and Deoksugung Palace. Deoksugung is the only palace open on Mondays and has a beautiful stone-wall road (Deoksugung Doldam-gil) alongside it. Admission is ₩1,000. The palace grounds are lovely in winter. Nearby Cheonggyecheon Stream is also walkable.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Euljiro area — a trendy neighborhood blending old industrial workshops with hip cafes and bars. Very popular with young Koreans and a great example of Seoul's urban renewal culture. Explore the unique atmosphere and grab dinner at one of the many affordable local restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market — kalguksu or haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) at a market restaurant (₩7,000–₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Euljiro local restaurant — try a hearty sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set meal (₩8,000–₩11,000)

day_by_day.notes: Namdaemun Market is best in the morning when it's most active. Bargaining is acceptable at clothing and accessory stalls. The Deoksugung stone wall road is one of Seoul's most romantic winter walks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park — a stunning mountain park right within Seoul city limits. Take the subway to Gupabal or Dobongsan station and hike one of the beginner-friendly trails. The winter scenery with snow-dusted granite peaks is spectacular. Entry to the park is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking or descend and explore the neighborhood at the base of the mountain. Visit a traditional Korean tea house near the park entrance to warm up with a cup of sikhye or yujacha (citron tea).
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major event — Koreans celebrate it as a romantic holiday. Head to Myeongdong or Gangnam for the festive atmosphere, Christmas lights, and street performances. Myeongdong Cathedral holds a special Christmas Eve mass open to all. The city is beautifully decorated.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — pack snacks for the hike
meals.lunch: Pack kimbap from a convenience store for the hike (₩1,500–₩3,000) or eat at a mountain trail restaurant
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — treat yourself to a slightly nicer Korean BBQ dinner in Myeongdong or a festive street food spread (₩15,000–₩20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Wear proper hiking shoes and warm layers for Bukhansan — trails can be icy in December. Crampons (아이젠, aizen) can be rented or bought cheaply near the trailhead. Christmas Eve in Seoul is magical — the city goes all out with decorations and events.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (free entry) and the Seoul Museum of History (free) nearby. These are less crowded than the major palaces and offer a peaceful Christmas morning. The museum has excellent exhibits on Seoul's history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gangnam district — explore the upscale Apgujeong and Garosu-gil (tree-lined street) areas. Browse the boutiques and cafes, and visit the SMTOWN COEX Artium — a K-pop entertainment complex with a free lobby area featuring K-pop merchandise and displays. The COEX Mall is one of Asia's largest underground malls.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the COEX Starfield Library — a stunning free public library inside COEX Mall, one of Seoul's most Instagrammable spots. Have dinner in the Gangnam area and enjoy the Christmas evening atmosphere before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: COEX food court — wide variety of Korean and international options at reasonable prices (₩8,000–₩12,000)
meals.dinner: Gangnam local restaurant — try samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) for a warming Christmas dinner (₩14,000–₩16,000)

day_by_day.notes: Most attractions are open on Christmas Day in Korea. The COEX Starfield Library is free and absolutely worth visiting — arrive early for the best photos. SMTOWN COEX Artium is a must for K-pop fans.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Itaewon and the surrounding Haebangchon (HBC) and Gyeongnidan-gil areas — multicultural neighborhoods with a unique mix of Korean and international culture. Explore the diverse street food, vintage shops, and the beautiful Bogwangdong neighborhood. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art if interested in Korean contemporary art (₩10,000 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to the nearby Namsan Mountain trails (free) for city views, or take the cable car. Visit the N Seoul Tower area again if you missed it earlier. Alternatively, head to the War Memorial of Korea in nearby Yongsan — a powerful and free museum with impressive outdoor exhibits of military equipment.
day_by_day.evening: Last big night out — head back to Hongdae or Myeongdong for final souvenir shopping and street food. Visit a norebang (Korean karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture experience — rooms typically cost ₩15,000–₩25,000 per hour split among the group.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store
meals.lunch: Itaewon area — try a Korean-fusion dish or affordable international food (₩9,000–₩13,000)
meals.dinner: Final Korean BBQ night — find a local 삼겹살 (samgyeopsal) restaurant for a proper farewell dinner (₩12,000–₩18,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial of Korea is free and one of Seoul's most underrated attractions. Norebang is an essential Korean cultural experience — look for 코인노래방 (coin karaoke) for an even cheaper option at ₩500–₩1,000 per song.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack up and check out of the hotel. If time allows, grab a last Korean breakfast at a nearby 해장국 (haejangguk) restaurant — a traditional hangover soup that's hearty and warming, perfect for a cold winter morning (₩8,000–₩10,000). Do any last-minute shopping at Bupyeong Underground Mall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX or bus from Bupyeong. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse the duty-free shops at the airport for last-minute Korean snacks, cosmetics, and gifts at competitive prices.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Local haejangguk restaurant near hotel (₩8,000–₩10,000)
meals.lunch: Airport food court or convenience store (₩8,000–₩12,000)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Return your T-money card at the airport for a refund of the remaining balance (minus ₩500 card deposit). Incheon Airport has excellent free facilities including a Korean Cultural Street on the 4th floor with free cultural performances and exhibits — worth exploring if you have a long wait. Pack any liquid K-beauty products in checked luggage.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or a limousine bus to Bupyeong station area. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24-hour convenience store (GS25 or CU) near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or hotteok for a quick, affordable bite after arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Dress warmly — December temperatures average around 3°C. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store or ticket machine for easy transit use throughout the trip. Exchange some cash (KRW) at the airport for better rates. Rest well tonight as Day 2 begins your full exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full day with a walk around Bupyeong Modoo Mall and Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center, one of Korea's largest underground markets. Browse K-fashion, accessories, and local goods. Get a feel for everyday Korean shopping culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Line 1) from Bupyeong to Incheon Chinatown and Sinpo International Market. Explore the colorful murals, Chinese-Korean fusion architecture, and the nearby Jayu Park — Korea's first Western-style park with great views of the port. Walk along the Open Port Area to see colonial-era buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sinpo International Market for evening street food. The market is famous for Sinpo-style dakgangjeong (sweet crispy fried chicken). Stroll the lit-up market stalls before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery like Paris Baguette — try a warm pastry and coffee (around 5,000–8,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) or tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork) at one of the authentic Chinese-Korean restaurants in Incheon Chinatown (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Sinpo dakgangjeong and tteokbokki at Sinpo International Market stalls (8,000–12,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers and a warm coat. The underground shopping center is a great way to stay warm while exploring. Bupyeong and Incheon Chinatown are easily connected by subway Line 1 — about 10 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Bupyeong to central Seoul via subway (Line 1 to Seoul Station, approx. 40–50 min). Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace, the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Catch the 10:00 AM Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the main gate. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from a nearby rental shop to enter the palace for free and take stunning photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Wander the narrow alleys, enjoy the contrast of old architecture against the modern city skyline, and visit small craft shops and galleries. Continue to Insadong for a leisurely afternoon browsing antique shops, tea houses, and K-culture souvenir stores.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil — an open-air courtyard mall with indie shops, art installations, and street food. Enjoy the festive December atmosphere with holiday lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store onigiri and coffee before departing.
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set meal (한정식 hanjeongsik lite) near Gyeongbokgung — try bibimbap or doenjang jjigae at a local restaurant (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a cozy restaurant in Insadong — try samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a mid-range BBQ spot (15,000–20,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Hanbok rental shops near the palace charge around 10,000–20,000 KRW for 2 hours. Bukchon Hanok Village asks visitors to be quiet out of respect for residents. Carry hand warmers — it will be cold walking outdoors.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Namsan Mountain and N Seoul Tower. Take the Namsan Cable Car up for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Visit the famous love lock fence and enjoy the crisp morning air. The tower area is magical in December with holiday decorations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and make your way to Myeongdong, Seoul's most famous shopping and beauty district. Explore K-beauty stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), fashion boutiques, and the lively street food scene. This is the heart of Korean pop culture commerce.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Myeongdong for the evening street food experience — one of the best in Seoul. The street vendors light up at night and the energy is electric even in winter.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near the hotel or at a café in Myeongdong before heading to Namsan.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Myeongdong — try hotteok (sweet pancake), eomuk (fish cake skewers), and gyeran-ppang (egg bread) from vendors (5,000–10,000 KRW total).
meals.dinner: Sit-down dinner at a Myeongdong restaurant — try naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles) or galbitang (short rib soup) to warm up (12,000–18,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower admission is around 21,000 KRW for adults. The cable car costs about 9,500 KRW round trip. Myeongdong is extremely popular — expect crowds on Friday evening. Olive Young is a must-visit for K-beauty products at reasonable prices.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). This UNESCO World Heritage Site is one of Seoul's most beautiful palaces, especially with winter frost on the traditional architecture. Book the Secret Garden tour in advance (guided tours only, limited spots).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace or head to the Jongno area to explore Tapgol Park and the traditional Jongno street. Visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with lanterns for the winter season.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a romantic evening walk along the illuminated waterway. The stream is lit up beautifully in winter and is a peaceful escape from the busy city streets.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a local sikdang (식당) near the hotel — try haejang-guk (hangover soup) or congee (juk) (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Changdeokgung — try a warm sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local restaurant (9,000–13,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner in the Jongno area — try dakhanmari (whole chicken in broth) at the famous Dakhanmari Alley near Dongdaemun (15,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours must be booked online in advance at the palace website. Tours are available in English. Wear very warm shoes as you'll be walking on stone paths. Cheonggyecheon Stream is free to visit and accessible from multiple subway stations.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's iconic futuristic building. Visit the design exhibitions and the surrounding Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. The area is fascinating for its blend of ancient city wall ruins and ultra-modern architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gwangjang Market, one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic traditional markets. This is a paradise for local food lovers — browse the fabric stalls and food hall packed with grandmothers cooking traditional dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Dongdaemun for the famous night shopping experience. Dongdaemun's fashion malls (Doota, Migliore) open late and are buzzing on Sunday evenings. Browse K-fashion at wholesale and retail prices.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel — try a Korean-style egg sandwich and Americano at a local café (6,000–9,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Iconic lunch at Gwangjang Market — must-try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini kimbap), and yukhoe (beef tartare). Budget around 10,000–15,000 KRW.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant near Dongdaemun — try gopchang (grilled intestines) or a hearty Korean stew (13,000–18,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: DDP admission varies by exhibition — check the website for current shows. Gwangjang Market is busiest at lunch and is a must for authentic Korean food culture. Dongdaemun shopping malls are open until 4–5 AM, so no rush in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway. Walk along the impressive 5.7 km fortress walls that encircle the old city. The winter scenery with frost on the stone walls is stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Haenggung Palace (Hwaseong Haenggung) inside the fortress grounds. Visit the Suwon Traditional Culture Center to learn about local crafts and history. Browse the traditional market street near the fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Spend a relaxed evening near the hotel, exploring the local Bupyeong neighborhood — visit a jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) for a warm, relaxing evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store before departing for Suwon.
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — the city's most famous dish — at a local restaurant near the fortress (15,000–25,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Jjimjilbang restaurant or a nearby Korean restaurant in Bupyeong — try kimchi jjigae or budae jjigae (army stew) (10,000–15,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress admission is around 1,000 KRW. Take subway Line 1 from Bupyeong directly to Suwon Station (about 50 minutes). A jjimjilbang entry costs around 10,000–15,000 KRW and includes access to hot baths, saunas, and rest areas — perfect for warming up after a cold day.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the epicenter of Korean youth culture, indie music, and street art. Explore the vibrant murals, quirky cafés, and K-pop culture shops. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or LINE Friends Store for fun K-culture experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area. The Ewha campus is architecturally stunning with its famous underground ECC building. Browse the trendy shops and cafés in Sinchon, popular with university students.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening — the neighborhood truly comes alive at night with buskers, live music, and street performances. Visit a norebang (karaoke room) for an authentic K-culture experience.

meals.breakfast: Trendy café breakfast in Hongdae — try a Korean-style brunch at one of the many Instagram-worthy cafés (8,000–13,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Hongdae — try tteokbokki and sundae (blood sausage) at a pojangmacha (street tent) or a casual restaurant (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Hongdae restaurant — try yangnyeom chicken (Korean fried chicken) with a cold Hite beer at a local chimaek spot (15,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Norebang rooms cost around 15,000–25,000 KRW per hour for a private room. Hongdae is very lively on weekday evenings — expect street performers even in December. The Trick Eye Museum costs around 15,000 KRW. Hongdae is accessible via subway Line 2 or the AREX airport line.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Itaewon and the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Korea's finest private art museums featuring both traditional Korean art and contemporary international works. The building itself, designed by three world-renowned architects, is a masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon's multicultural neighborhood — browse the international restaurants, vintage clothing shops, and antique stores on Antique Furniture Street. Walk up to Haebangchon (HBC) for a more local, artsy vibe with independent cafés and boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam district for the evening. Visit COEX Mall — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls — and the famous COEX Starfield Library, a stunning public library inside the mall. Browse the bookstore and enjoy the festive Christmas decorations.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near the hotel before heading out — try a warm bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a local restaurant (9,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: International lunch in Itaewon — try a Korean-Mexican fusion burrito or a Middle Eastern shawarma for a multicultural experience (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Gangnam — try a modern Korean restaurant or a trendy ramen shop near COEX (13,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Leeum Museum admission is around 10,000 KRW. COEX Starfield Library is free to visit and is one of Seoul's most photogenic spots. Gangnam is accessible via subway Line 2. The area will be beautifully decorated for Christmas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park for a morning winter hike. The mountain park sits within Seoul city limits and offers spectacular views of the snow-dusted peaks and the city below. Choose a beginner-friendly trail like the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and head to Myeongdong Cathedral — Seoul's most iconic Catholic church, beautifully lit for Christmas Eve. The area around the cathedral will be festively decorated. Browse the Christmas markets and enjoy the holiday atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Christmas Eve in Seoul — the city goes all out with lights and celebrations. Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream or City Hall Plaza for the Christmas light festival. Many young Koreans celebrate Christmas Eve like Valentine's Day, making the city especially lively.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike — convenience store kimbap and hot coffee or a quick meal near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Post-hike warm meal near Bukhansan — try a hearty doenjang jjigae or kimchi jjigae at a mountain restaurant (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner — treat yourself to a Korean BBQ restaurant in Myeongdong or a nice Korean fusion restaurant (20,000–30,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan National Park is free to enter. Wear proper hiking boots and warm layers — trails can be icy in December. Bring crampons or ice grips for shoes if possible. Christmas Eve in Seoul is very romantic and festive — the city is beautifully illuminated. Book dinner in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (less crowded than Gyeongbokgung) and the Seoul Museum of History next door. Learn about Seoul's transformation from ancient Joseon capital to modern megacity through fascinating exhibits. The museum is free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming neighborhood of traditional hanok houses converted into cafés, art galleries, and boutiques. This is a quieter, more authentic alternative to Bukchon. Visit the Yun Dong-ju Literary Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lotte World Tower in Jamsil for the evening. Visit the Sky Observatory on the 117th–123rd floors for breathtaking nighttime views of Seoul. The tower and surrounding Lotte World Mall are spectacularly lit for Christmas.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning café breakfast — try a festive holiday drink and pastry at a cozy Seochon café (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Seochon Village — try a traditional Korean meal at a hanok café-restaurant (12,000–18,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner near Lotte World — try a nice Korean or international restaurant in the Jamsil area (20,000–30,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Seoul Museum of History is free. Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory costs around 27,000 KRW. Many restaurants may have special Christmas menus — check in advance. Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea, so some smaller shops may be closed but major attractions remain open.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of the largest museums in Asia, with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning thousands of years. The museum is free and takes 2–3 hours to explore properly. Don't miss the Goryeo celadon and Joseon white porcelain collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the War Memorial of Korea nearby — a powerful and moving museum documenting Korea's military history, including the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits with tanks, aircraft, and warships are impressive even in winter. Free admission.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your last full evening in the Yongsan Electronics Market or head back to a favorite neighborhood for final shopping and souvenir hunting. Visit a traditional Korean tea house for a warm, reflective end to your trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery near the hotel for a relaxed morning start.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the National Museum of Korea's cafeteria or a nearby restaurant — try a Korean set meal (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a memorable Korean meal. Try a traditional Korean royal cuisine restaurant or a premium Korean BBQ spot (25,000–35,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Both the National Museum of Korea and the War Memorial are free. The National Museum is closed on Mondays. Allow at least 2 hours for each museum. This is a great day for reflection on Korean history and culture before your trip ends. Pack souvenirs tonight to prepare for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take a leisurely walk around the Bupyeong neighborhood. Visit a local juk (porridge) restaurant for a light, healthy Korean breakfast. Do any last-minute shopping at Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit a nearby café for a final Korean coffee experience. Pack and check out of the hotel. Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX or limousine bus (allow 60–90 minutes from Bupyeong). Use remaining KRW at the airport duty-free shops.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of K-culture, incredible food, and unforgettable experiences in Seoul and Incheon.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — try juk (rice porridge) with various toppings at a local porridge restaurant (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport — try a Korean meal at one of the many airport restaurants before departure (12,000–18,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Toyoko Inn is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the hotel. Incheon Airport is one of the world's best airports with excellent shopping, dining, and cultural experiences (free Korean cultural performances and craft workshops in the transit area). Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. T-money card can be refunded at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Joseon-era royal palace while dressed in traditional Hanbok attire. Hanbok rental shops are located just outside the palace gates, making it easy to combine both activities. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry. Ideal for Day 2 or 3 after settling in, and best done in the morning to avoid crowds. Stay nearby in Jongno-gu to walk directly to the palace.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). The market is lively and authentic, offering a true local food experience without tourist markup. Book a guided food tour or explore independently. Stay in Jongno-gu or Euljiro for easy access.

experiences.name: Hongdae K-Culture & Street Performance Walk
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Seoul's vibrant K-pop and youth culture hub. Hongdae is packed with indie music venues, K-pop dance studios offering drop-in classes, street performers, quirky cafes, and K-beauty shops. Join a K-pop dance class at a local studio for around $15–20, then explore the nightlife and street art. This area is best experienced in the late afternoon through evening when energy peaks.

experiences.name: Insadong Teahouse & Craft Culture Experience
experiences.description: Wander through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and galleries. Visit Ssamziegil, an artsy courtyard mall with local designers and handmade goods. Stop at a traditional Korean tea house to try omija tea or sikhye. This culturally rich neighborhood is walkable from Gyeongbokgung and Gwangjang Market, making it perfect for a combined day out. Ideal for mid-trip exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.evening: Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and take the AREX Express Train or private airport transfer to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. Light late-night snack near the hotel if hungry.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal
meals.lunch: In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snack or 24-hour Korean ramen shop near Bupyeong station (Bupyeong is known for its underground shopping and late-night eateries)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30 KST. Allow 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and transfer. Bupyeong station area has 24-hour convenience stores and pojangmacha (street food stalls). Rest well — the itinerary begins properly tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel breakfast, then explore Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center — one of Korea's largest underground malls, great for K-beauty products, fashion, and local goods. Stroll around Bupyeong-gu neighborhood to acclimate to the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway from Bupyeong to central Seoul (approx. 40 min). Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental — dress in traditional Hanbok attire and explore the iconic Joseon-era royal palace. Stroll through the palace grounds, visit Gyeonghoeru Pavilion, and enjoy the winter atmosphere with light snow possibilities.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bukchon Hanok Village for a twilight walk through preserved traditional Korean houses. Enjoy the atmospheric lantern-lit alleyways in the cold winter evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café in Bupyeong
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang — legendary ginseng chicken soup restaurant near Gyeongbokgung, perfect for warming up in winter
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul (2 Michelin stars) in Gangnam — modern Korean cuisine with premium tasting menus showcasing elevated Korean flavors

day_by_day.notes: Hanbok rental shops near Gyeongbokgung open around 9–10am. Book Jungsik in advance as it fills up quickly. Dress in warm layers under the Hanbok — December temperatures average 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The winter-bare trees and frozen ponds create a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere. Guided tours of the Secret Garden are available in English.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Insadong Teahouse & Craft Culture Experience — wander through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and galleries. Visit Ssamziegil courtyard for artisan goods and unique Korean souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Cheonggyecheon Stream, beautifully lit in the evening. Then head to the Jongno area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Bora in Insadong — famous for its purple taro lattes and Korean-inspired pastries
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang — award-winning Buddhist temple cuisine restaurant near Insadong, offering a serene and refined dining experience
meals.dinner: Mingles (1 Michelin star) — innovative Korean cuisine blending traditional and contemporary techniques in a sophisticated setting

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours at Changdeokgung require advance booking and run at set times. Insadong is walkable from the palace. Cheonggyecheon Stream is beautifully illuminated in winter evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour — dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), and yukhoe (Korean beef tartare). Arrive early for the freshest experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark. Browse design exhibitions, visit the Seoul Museum of Design, and explore the surrounding fashion district. Check out the Dongdaemun History & Culture Park nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Namsan Seoul Tower via cable car for panoramic night views of the glittering Seoul skyline. Visit the observation deck and enjoy the romantic lock wall.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market street food feast — budget extra time to sample multiple stalls including the famous raw beef yukhoe and fresh bindaetteok
meals.dinner: Gaon (3 Michelin stars) — the pinnacle of Korean fine dining, offering an exquisite royal court cuisine-inspired tasting menu with exceptional service

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is most vibrant in the morning. Book Gaon well in advance — it is one of Seoul's most prestigious restaurants. Namsan Tower cable car runs until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with an extraordinary collection of Korean artifacts spanning 5,000 years of history. Explore the permanent galleries at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon and the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — a world-class private museum housing both traditional Korean art and contemporary international works in a stunning building designed by three architectural legends.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hongdae K-Culture & Street Performance Walk — immerse yourself in Seoul's vibrant K-pop and youth culture hub. Hongdae is packed with indie music venues, street performers, K-pop merchandise stores, and trendy cafés. Experience the electric Saturday night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Anthracite Coffee Roasters in Itaewon — specialty coffee in a converted factory space, a Seoul institution
meals.lunch: Vatos Urban Tacos in Itaewon — beloved fusion restaurant blending Korean and Mexican flavors with premium ingredients
meals.dinner: Maple Tree House in Itaewon — premium Korean BBQ with USDA prime and Hanwoo beef, elegant private dining rooms

day_by_day.notes: Leeum Museum may require advance ticket booking for special exhibitions. Hongdae is most vibrant after 7pm on weekends with street performers and pop-up events. Dress warmly for outdoor street performances.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Namsangol Hanok Village — a beautifully restored traditional Korean village at the foot of Namsan Mountain. Explore the five restored aristocratic homes, traditional gardens, and cultural performances.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Myeongdong — Seoul's premier shopping and beauty district. Explore flagship K-beauty stores (Sulwhasoo, Innisfree, Amorepacific), luxury department stores (Lotte, Shinsegae), and sample street food along the main boulevard.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Korean performance — book tickets for the National Theater of Korea or a Nanta cooking performance show for an entertaining cultural evening.

meals.breakfast: Egg Drop in Myeongdong — premium egg sandwich café beloved by locals and visitors
meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja — legendary hand-made noodle and dumpling restaurant, a Seoul institution since 1966
meals.dinner: Dooreyoo (1 Michelin star) — refined Korean cuisine with a focus on seasonal ingredients and traditional fermentation techniques

day_by_day.notes: Namsangol Hanok Village is free to enter and offers cultural programs on weekends. Myeongdong is extremely busy on Sundays — visit flagship beauty stores early. Book performance tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul. Observe morning rituals, admire the ancient trees, and experience the serene contrast between the temple and the bustling city. Explore the Buddhist cultural center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming neighborhood of narrow alleyways, independent galleries, artisan workshops, and traditional hanok cafés. Visit the Gyeomjae Jeong Seon Memorial Hall and browse local art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Gwanghwamun Square area — see the illuminated statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Enjoy the winter light installations that typically decorate the square during December.

meals.breakfast: Café Onion Anguk — a beautifully renovated hanok café serving artisan pastries and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gwanghwamun Gukbap — premium Korean rice soup restaurant beloved by locals for its rich, slow-cooked broth
meals.dinner: La Yeon (3 Michelin stars) at The Shilla Hotel — extraordinary Korean fine dining with breathtaking city views from the 23rd floor

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is particularly atmospheric in the early morning. Seochon Village is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. La Yeon requires advance reservation and smart dress code.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site just 30 minutes from Seoul by subway. Walk the 5.7km fortress walls, visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace, and enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Suwon — visit the Korean Folk Village nearby for an immersive experience of traditional Korean rural life, crafts, and seasonal performances.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and head to Gangnam district — explore the upscale Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Cheongdam-dong luxury fashion district, home to flagship Korean designer boutiques and international luxury brands.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi — Suwon is famous for its distinctive short-rib BBQ style; dine at a traditional galbi restaurant in the city center
meals.dinner: Dosa in Cheongdam-dong — sophisticated modern Korean restaurant in the heart of Gangnam's luxury district

day_by_day.notes: Take Line 1 subway directly to Suwon Station (approx. 50 min from Seoul). The fortress walk takes 2–3 hours. Korean Folk Village is a 15-minute taxi from Suwon Station. Return to Seoul by 6pm for evening activities.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan — a powerful and comprehensive museum documenting Korea's military history. The outdoor exhibition of aircraft, tanks, and warships is impressive even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Hannam-dong neighborhood — Seoul's most fashionable enclave with concept stores, art galleries, and design studios. Visit the Hannam-dong antique furniture district and browse independent boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Korean tea ceremony at O'sulloc Tea House or a private tea ceremony studio in Insadong. Then enjoy a night walk along the Han River at Banpo Bridge to see the famous Rainbow Fountain (seasonal — check availability in December).

meals.breakfast: Fritz Coffee Company in Mapo — one of Seoul's most celebrated specialty coffee roasters
meals.lunch: Hannam-dong Burger — premium Korean-style gourmet burger at one of Hannam's trendy lunch spots
meals.dinner: Soigné (1 Michelin star) — avant-garde tasting menu restaurant in Hannam-dong, blending Korean ingredients with European techniques

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial is free to enter. Hannam-dong is best explored on foot. Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain may not operate in December due to cold — confirm in advance. Soigné requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World — Asia's largest indoor theme park for a festive Christmas Eve experience. Enjoy the elaborate Christmas decorations, ice skating rink, and indoor attractions. Alternatively, visit the adjacent Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory for stunning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jamsil and the COEX Mall — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls. Visit the famous Starfield Library inside COEX, browse luxury boutiques, and explore the aquarium.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve special dinner and celebration. Experience Seoul's festive atmosphere in Myeongdong or Gangnam, where streets are beautifully decorated with Christmas lights and live performances.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lotte World Food Court or a café inside Lotte World Tower
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at Nobu Seoul in Lotte World Tower — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion with premium ingredients and festive seasonal menu

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the most festive nights in Seoul — the city transforms with lights and celebrations. Book Christmas Eve dinner well in advance. Lotte World Tower observation deck offers spectacular night views of the city.

day_by_day.morning: Peaceful Christmas morning walk in Olympic Park — one of Seoul's most beautiful parks, featuring outdoor sculptures, walking paths, and the historic Mongchontoseong earthen fortress. Enjoy the crisp winter air and serene atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seoul Arts Center in Seocho — explore the galleries, outdoor sculpture garden, and check for special Christmas Day performances or exhibitions. Browse the arts and crafts market if available.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert or traditional Korean performance at the Seoul Arts Center or National Theater of Korea — many venues host special Christmas Day performances.

meals.breakfast: Tartine Bakery Seoul in Gangnam — premium artisan bakery for a special Christmas morning treat
meals.lunch: Hanwoo Dining Woo Lae Oak — one of Seoul's most historic Korean BBQ restaurants, established in 1946, serving premium Hanwoo beef
meals.dinner: Mosu Seoul (2 Michelin stars) — intimate and innovative Korean tasting menu with exceptional seasonal ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Many attractions have reduced hours on Christmas Day — confirm opening times in advance. Seoul Arts Center and National Theater of Korea typically have special holiday programming. Book dinner reservations well ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park — Seoul's stunning mountain national park offering winter hiking trails with snow-dusted peaks. Take the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail for panoramic views of Seoul. Dress in proper winter hiking gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the Dongdaemun area for a final shopping session. Explore the Dongdaemun Design Plaza market and pick up last-minute Korean souvenirs, fashion, and K-beauty products.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in Gangnam — explore the vibrant nightlife of Apgujeong and Cheongdam-dong. Visit a rooftop bar for final panoramic views of Seoul's glittering skyline.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store kimbap and hot coffee before the hike — a quintessential Korean hiking tradition
meals.lunch: Post-hike warm meal at a traditional doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean stew) restaurant near Bukhansan
meals.dinner: Kwon Sooksoo — elegant Korean fine dining in Cheongdam-dong, celebrating traditional Korean flavors with refined modern presentation for a memorable farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan requires proper winter hiking boots and warm layers. Trails can be icy — bring microspikes if available. The hike to Baegundae Peak takes approximately 3–4 hours round trip. Return to the city by early afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — revisit a favorite neighborhood or café for a leisurely breakfast. Last-minute shopping at a nearby convenience store or pharmacy for Korean skincare products and snacks to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and transfer to Incheon International Airport. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for check-in, duty-free shopping, and security. Incheon Airport's duty-free zone is world-class — browse Korean cosmetics, food gifts, and luxury goods.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Korean culture, cuisine, and luxury experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast at a local restaurant near the hotel — doenjang jjigae, steamed rice, and banchan (side dishes) for an authentic send-off
meals.lunch: Incheon Airport — dine at one of the premium airport restaurants such as Korean Air's Morning Calm lounge or a sit-down Korean restaurant in the departure terminal
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11am — store luggage at the hotel if needed for a final morning activity. The AREX Express Train from Bupyeong to Incheon Airport takes approximately 30–40 minutes. Incheon Airport is consistently rated the world's best airport — arrive early to enjoy the duty-free experience.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX
